properties.description: Before processing blob KZG commitments, the block proposer must provide a beacon block body containing blob_kzg_commitments via the boundary edge EDGE-EXT-BLOCK-ARRIVAL. The block must be well-formed and signed.
properties.formal_expression: forall block in received_blocks: is_signed(block) AND has_field(block.body, blob_kzg_commitments)

properties.description: Before converting commitments to versioned hashes, the commitment count must have been validated to not exceed MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK (6).
After versioned hash validation, all beacon block blob commitments must match the corresponding execution payload blob transaction commitments exactly.
After caching blob gas metrics, the execution payload header must contain accurate blob_gas_used and excess_blob_gas values from the execution payload.
The number of blob KZG commitments in any valid block must never exceed MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK (6) at any point in the processing pipeline.
Each versioned hash must be prefixed with VERSIONED_HASH_VERSION_KZG (0x01) throughout the entire processing lifecycle.
properties.formal_expression: invariant: forall vh in versioned_hashes: vh[0] == 0x01

properties.description: Before setting participation flags, the attestation must have passed the extended inclusion window check: attestation.slot + MIN_ATTESTATION_INCLUSION_DELAY <= current_slot.
After processing a valid attestation with correct target, TIMELY_TARGET_FLAG must be set regardless of inclusion delay.
properties.formal_expression: post(ACTION-SET-PARTICIPATION-FLAGS) => if correct_target then TIMELY_TARGET_FLAG is set

properties.description: Attestations outside the valid inclusion window (target epoch and next epoch per EIP-7045) must always be rejected and must never reach the participation flag setting stage.
After an attestation is rejected due to inclusion window violation, no participation flags are modified in the beacon state.

Before sending NewPayloadRequest to the execution engine via boundary edge EDGE-EL-CALL, the request must contain execution_payload, versioned_hashes derived from blob commitments, and parent_beacon_block_root.
properties.formal_expression: pre(ACTION-NOTIFY-NEW-PAYLOAD) => request.has(execution_payload) AND request.has(versioned_hashes) AND request.has(parent_beacon_block_root)

properties.description: After the execution engine returns VALID, the payload must be considered validated and state transition should proceed. After INVALID, the block must be rejected.
properties.formal_expression: post(ACTION-NOTIFY-NEW-PAYLOAD) => (result == VALID => STATE-PAYLOAD-VALIDATED) AND (result == INVALID => STATE-PAYLOAD-INVALID)

properties.description: The NewPayloadRequest must always include versioned hashes that are consistent with the beacon block's blob KZG commitments throughout the CL-EL boundary.
The parent_beacon_block_root (EIP-4788) in the NewPayloadRequest must match the actual parent beacon block root at all times.
Before dequeuing validators for activation, the activation churn limit must be computed as min(MAX_PER_EPOCH_ACTIVATION_CHURN_LIMIT, computed_churn_limit).
After dequeuing, the number of newly activated validators must not exceed the computed activation churn limit (capped at 8).
The per-epoch activation count must never exceed MAX_PER_EPOCH_ACTIVATION_CHURN_LIMIT (8) regardless of the total validator set size.
Before validating a voluntary exit signature, the exit message must use CAPELLA_FORK_VERSION for domain computation, not the current fork version.
After successful exit signature validation, the validator must begin the exit process and its exit_epoch must be set.
Exit signatures must always be validated against CAPELLA_FORK_VERSION domain, ensuring perpetual validity across future fork upgrades.
Before submitting a BLSToExecutionChange claim, the validator must provide a properly signed message via boundary edge EDGE-VALIDATOR-SUBMIT.
Before loading a broadcast file into a beacon node via boundary edge EDGE-OPERATOR-LOAD, the node operator must have obtained a verified broadcast file.
After Capella fork activation triggers broadcast, all verified messages from the broadcast file must be transmitted exactly once to the P2P network.
properties.formal_expression: post(ACTION-BROADCAST-AT-CAPELLA) => forall msg in broadcast_file: broadcast_count(msg) == 1

properties.description: Throughout the broadcast lifecycle, each validator index must have at most one BLSToExecutionChange message in the system.
After signature verification succeeds, the claim must be accepted into the broadcast file with its cryptographic validity confirmed.
properties.formal_expression: post(ACTION-VERIFY-SIGNATURE) => claim in broadcast_file AND bls_verify(claim) == true

properties.description: Before claim validation begins, the submitter must provide a claim file via boundary edge EDGE-CLAIM-SUBMIT with the expected validatorIndex.json format.
After full validation, an accepted claim must have passed all four checks: filename format, validator active status, BLS signature, and single operation per validator.
properties.formal_expression: post(STATE-CLAIM-ACCEPTED) => filename_valid AND validator_active AND bls_sig_valid AND single_op_per_validator

properties.description: A claim that fails any single validation step must be rejected and must never reach STATE-CLAIM-ACCEPTED.
properties.formal_expression: invariant: (filename_invalid OR validator_inactive OR sig_invalid OR duplicate_op) => claim in STATE-CLAIM-REJECTED

properties.description: Validation steps must execute in strict order: filename, then validator active check, then BLS signature, then single operation check.
Before checking against the broadcast file, a BLSToExecutionChange message must be received from a P2P peer via boundary edge EDGE-PEER-MESSAGE.
After detecting a conflict with the broadcast file, the message must be rejected and dropped, never propagated to other peers.
properties.formal_expression: post(STATE-MESSAGE-CONFLICTS) => message in STATE-MESSAGE-DROPPED AND NOT propagated(message)

properties.description: Messages for validators without broadcast file entries must be accepted and propagated normally, providing no filtering protection.
Broadcast file filtering must persist throughout the node's operation after Capella activation to prevent late-arriving attack messages.
Before checking fork block, the system must have access to the current block number and the configured Istanbul activation block number.
After Istanbul activation, all six bundled EIPs (EIP-152, EIP-1108, EIP-1344, EIP-1884, EIP-2028, EIP-2200) must be simultaneously active.
properties.formal_expression: post(STATE-ISTANBUL-ACTIVATED) => all_active([EIP152, EIP1108, EIP1344, EIP1884, EIP2028, EIP2200])

properties.description: Fork activation is irreversible: once block number >= activation block, the system must never revert to pre-Istanbul rules.
Post-Istanbul, gas costs must use the updated schedule: alt_bn128 reduced costs, SLOAD/BALANCE/EXTCODE increased costs, calldata reduced costs.
After gas calculation, if remaining gas is insufficient, execution must halt with out-of-gas error and all state changes reverted.
Before gas calculation, the fork state must be determined to select the correct gas schedule (pre or post Istanbul).
Before routing to a specific precompile execution, the precompile address must be validated as a recognized precompile address including the new 0x09 Blake2b.
After successful execution of any bn128 precompile, the result must be a valid curve point and gas must be charged at reduced Istanbul rates.
Invalid precompile addresses or malformed input must always result in STATE-PRECOMPILE-FAILED, never in partial execution.
Before executing apply_dao(), the current block number must exactly equal the fork activation block (1,920,000).
After all 117 DAO accounts are processed, each account must have zero balance and the recovery contract must hold the sum of all transferred balances.
properties.formal_expression: post(STATE-POST-FORK-STATE) => forall a in DAO_ACCOUNTS: balance(a) == 0 AND balance(DAO_RECOVERY) == sum(original_balances)

properties.description: During DAO account iteration, total ETH in the system must be conserved: sum of all DAO account balances plus recovery contract balance must remain constant.
The apply_dao() function must be idempotent; re-execution must not alter state if balances are already zero.
Before header validation, the block header must arrive from a block producer via boundary edge EDGE-EXT-HEADER.
For blocks within the 10-block fork window, the extra_data field must contain b'dao-hard-fork' or the block must be rejected.
properties.formal_expression: post(ACTION-CHECK-EXTRA-DATA) => (extra_data == b'dao-hard-fork' => STATE-EXTRA-DATA-VALID) AND (extra_data != b'dao-hard-fork' => STATE-EXTRA-DATA-INVALID)

properties.description: Blocks outside the fork window must bypass the extra_data check and proceed directly to standard header validation.
properties.formal_expression: invariant: block.number < fork_block OR block.number >= fork_block + 10 => skip_extra_data_check

properties.description: Before a DAO token holder can call withdraw() via boundary edge EDGE-USER-WITHDRAW, they must hold DAO tokens.
After successful withdrawal, the user must receive ETH proportional to their DAO token holdings.
The total ETH withdrawn from the recovery contract must never exceed the total ETH transferred in from DAO accounts.
Before BLS precompile execution, the EVM execution context must provide calldata and gas limit via boundary edge EDGE-EVM-CALL-PRECOMPILE.
After validation failure, the precompile must consume all supplied gas and return an error.
Only inputs that pass all three validation stages (field element, on-curve, subgroup) may reach the cryptographic execution stage.
properties.formal_expression: invariant: STATE-VALIDATION-PASSED => field_valid AND curve_valid AND (subgroup_valid OR op_type in {ADD})

properties.description: After successful cryptographic operation, the encoded output must be in canonical format matching the expected output size for the operation type.
Before input validation, raw calldata must be received from the EVM via boundary edge EDGE-RECEIVE-INPUT.
After Fp encoding validation, all field elements must have top 16 bytes zero and value strictly less than the BLS12-381 field modulus p.
properties.formal_expression: post(ACTION-CHECK-FP-ENCODING) => forall fp: fp[0:16] == 0x00 AND uint(fp) < p

properties.description: Empty input for MSM and pairing operations must always be rejected as an error.
properties.formal_expression: invariant: (op_type in {MSM, PAIRING} AND input_length == 0) => STATE-INPUT-EMPTY

properties.description: Points not on the curve must never pass subgroup checking; curve membership is a prerequisite for subgroup checking.
Before gas calculation, the EVM gas context must provide available gas and input size via boundary edge EDGE-START-GAS-CALC.
After MSM gas calculation, the cost must equal (k * base_cost * discount) / 1000 where discount is looked up from the discount table based on k.
Gas cost must always be deducted before operation execution; insufficient gas must prevent operation from starting.
Before any BLS operation, untrusted input from a potentially malicious smart contract must be sanitized via boundary edge EDGE-RECEIVE-UNTRUSTED.
After sanitization, trusted input must have passed all validation rules; malformed input must be rejected.
G1ADD and G2ADD operations must explicitly skip subgroup checking, accepting any on-curve point including non-subgroup points.
Gas metering must always bound resource consumption for all BLS operations to prevent denial-of-service attacks.
properties.formal_expression: invariant: forall bls_op: gas_metered(bls_op) AND execution_time <= f(gas_limit)

properties.description: Before applying post-Tangerine Whistle gas costs, the block number must be >= 2,463,000.
After post-Tangerine EXTCODESIZE execution, exactly 700 gas must be deducted (up from 20).
Post-Tangerine Whistle, SELFDESTRUCT with a new beneficiary account must always cost base (5000) plus new account penalty (25000) gas.
All IO-heavy opcode gas costs must be consistently applied across all execution contexts within the same block.
properties.formal_expression: invariant: forall tx in block: gas_schedule(tx) == gas_schedule(block)

properties.description: Before initiating a child call, the parent context must have sufficient gas to cover extra_gas costs.
After gas allocation, the child context must receive at most gas - (gas // 64), enforcing the 63/64 rule.
The 63/64 gas rule must limit maximum call depth, preventing unbounded recursion that could cause stack overflow.
Before SELFDESTRUCT executes, the beneficiary account existence must be checked to determine the applicable gas cost.
After SELFDESTRUCT completes, the contract must be marked for deletion and its entire balance transferred to the beneficiary.
New account penalty (25000 gas) must only apply when the beneficiary does not exist in state; existing beneficiaries incur only base cost (5000).
Before batch submission, the DApp must provide batch calls and flow control parameters via boundary edge EDGE-DAPP-SUBMIT.
After all calls succeed, the batch must reach confirmed status (code 200) with all call receipts present.
properties.formal_expression: post(STATE-BATCH-CONFIRMED) => status_code == 200 AND forall call: receipt(call).present

properties.description: Batch status codes must be monotonically progressing: pending (100) to partial (102) to terminal states (200/207/500/600).
Calls within a batch must execute in order; no call may execute before all preceding calls have been attempted.
properties.formal_expression: invariant: forall i < j: execution_time(call[i]) <= execution_time(call[j])

properties.description: Before setting atomicity mode, the DApp must specify the requested level via boundary edge EDGE-PARSE-REQUEST.
After capability check, if the wallet cannot support the requested atomicity level, an UNSUPPORTED_LEVEL error must be returned.
Strict atomicity must guarantee that calls remain atomic even during block reorgs; loose atomicity guarantees atomicity only absent reorgs.
properties.formal_expression: invariant: strict => atomic_under_reorg AND loose => atomic_without_reorg

properties.description: Before checking the failure mode, a call must have actually failed execution.
After rollback mode triggers, the entire batch must be reverted with no partial state changes persisting.
properties.formal_expression: post(ACTION-REVERT-BATCH) => forall call in batch: state_changes(call) == REVERTED

properties.description: The three failure modes (rollback, halt, continue) must be mutually exclusive; exactly one must be selected per failed call.
properties.formal_expression: invariant: exactly_one(MODE-ROLLBACK, MODE-HALT, MODE-CONTINUE) for each failed call

properties.description: Before flow control validation, a request must be received with defined structure.
After validation, rollback mode with none atomicity must be rejected as incompatible.
Call-scope flow control capabilities must never be used without batch-scope capabilities being present.
Before processing block query, an RPC client must send an eth_getBlockByNumber request via boundary edge EDGE-CLIENT-REQUEST.
After determining a block is post-EIP-1559, the response must include the baseFee field; pre-1559 blocks must omit it.
After response construction, the response must be returned to the requesting RPC client via boundary edge EDGE-RETURN-RESPONSE.
The fork block number used for baseFee inclusion decisions must be consistent across all RPC queries from the same node.
properties.formal_expression: invariant: fork_block_number == config.EIP1559_FORK_BLOCK for all queries

properties.description: Before baseFee presence validation, the block data must be loaded from storage.
After validation, a post-1559 block missing its baseFee field must fail validation.
The baseFee exposed via RPC must exactly match the baseFee stored in the block header with no transformation other than hex encoding.
Before processing an ENRRequest, the request must arrive from a peer node via boundary edge EDGE-RECEIVE-ENR-REQUEST.
After validation succeeds, an ENRResponse containing the current signed ENR must be sent back to the requesting peer via boundary edge EDGE-RESPONSE-TO-PEER.
Rejected ENRRequests (expired or no ping history) must never generate an ENRResponse.
Before extracting ENR sequence number, a ping packet must be received from a peer via boundary edge EDGE-RECEIVE-PING.
After sequence comparison, if the received seq > cached seq, the local ENR cache must be marked outdated triggering an ENRRequest.
Every ping received must generate a pong response with the node's current enr-seq, regardless of the sequence comparison result.
Before validating an ENRResponse, it must arrive from a peer via boundary edge EDGE-RECEIVE-ENR-RESPONSE.
After successful ENR validation (hash match and signature valid), the local node table must be updated with the validated ENR.
ENR records with invalid signatures must never be stored in the node table.

Before authorizing an ENRRequest, the requester must have established a prior ping exchange and the request must not be expired, checked via boundary edge EDGE-INCOMING-REQUEST from an untrusted peer.
After detecting no prior ping exchange, the ENRRequest must be silently dropped to prevent amplification attacks.
The amplification attack prevention mechanism must be enforced for all ENRRequests; no request may bypass the ping history check.
Before transaction decoding, raw transaction bytes must be received from an external source via boundary edge EDGE-RECEIVE-TX.
After sender recovery, the recovered address must be a valid 20-byte Ethereum address derived from the transaction signature.
properties.formal_expression: post(ACTION-RECOVER-SENDER) => len(sender) == 20 AND sender == ecrecover(signing_hash, v, r, s)

properties.description: The transaction processing pipeline must follow strict ordering: decode, recover sender, validate, hash. No step may be skipped.
Before type byte extraction, a typed transaction must be received with at least one byte.
Type byte discrimination must be exhaustive: 0x01 maps to AccessList, 0x02 to FeeMarket, 0x03 to Blob, >= 0xC0 to Legacy. Unknown types must be rejected.
properties.formal_expression: invariant: type_byte in {0x01, 0x02, 0x03} OR type_byte >= 0xC0 OR tx_rejected

properties.description: After intrinsic gas computation, the total must include base cost (21000) plus data costs plus optional creation and access list costs.
Transactions with gas limit below intrinsic gas must always be rejected; they must never proceed to execution.
Before SECP256K1 recovery, the r and s signature values must be validated to be within the curve order bounds.
properties.formal_expression: pre(ACTION-SECP256K1-RECOVER) => 0 < r < SECP256K1_N AND 0 < s < SECP256K1_N

properties.description: After address derivation, the sender address must be the last 20 bytes of Keccak256 of the recovered uncompressed public key.
Invalid signature bounds must prevent any further processing; the recovery pipeline must halt at the bounds check.
Before gas sufficiency check, the transaction must be decoded with sender recovered.
After full validation, a validated transaction must have sufficient gas, valid nonce (< 2^64-1), and init code within MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE.
properties.formal_expression: post(STATE-TX-FULLY-VALIDATED) => gas_sufficient AND nonce < 2^64-1 AND (is_creation => data.length <= 49152)

properties.description: Validation must follow strict ordering: gas check, then nonce check, then init code check. Early failures must prevent subsequent checks.
